summary: Adds an IEJoin (inequality join) operator, rule, and linq4j enumerator for inner joins with two or more cross-input inequality predicates, and registers the rule in the default Enumerable rule sets.

tests.evidence: New operator and algorithm; mihaibudiu said the EnumerableIEJoinTest cases were hard to review and asked why the outputs are correct (a hard-coded 600 was replaced by a nested-loop count), and asked what happens when both comparisons use the same field, which had no test until then.

user_docs.evidence: New rule enters the default rule sets (EnumerableRules, Programs), changing plans users see, but Calcite does not document individual enumerable rules on its site.

doc_comments.evidence: Reviewer asked for Javadoc on IEJoinEnumerator and its non-obvious fields and on the test helpers, flagged a copy-pasted comment in EnumerableIEJoin, and asked that the algorithm be explained without assuming readers know the paper.

change_description.evidence: Title matches the Jira (CALCITE-7755) and the description explains the algorithm and scope; no issue raised.

performance.evidence: New join algorithm with its own computeSelfCost (2*nLogN + rows) that now competes with nested-loop join in default plans; mihaibudiu asked whether it is still more efficient with a residual Calc, and no benchmark backs the cost model.

security.evidence: No auth, parsing, or credential code; memory use of materialized inputs is comparable to existing hash and merge joins.

backward_compat.evidence: ENUMERABLE_IE_JOIN_RULE is added to EnumerableRules.ENUMERABLE_RULES and Programs, so existing queries change plans (CombineRelOptRulesTest.xml switches NestedLoopJoin to IEJoin) and row order changes; the maintainer blamed later CI failures on non-deterministic tests.

concurrency.evidence: IEJoinEnumerator reads and closes both input enumerators in try-with-resources and clears state in close(); nothing shared.

error_model.evidence: New IllegalArgumentException paths in the EnumerableIEJoin constructor, copy(), and EnumerableDefaults.ieJoin with messages naming the offending types or operator; unremarkable.

correctness.evidence: Non-trivial union-array algorithm with strict/non-strict tie-breaks and null handling; reviewer asked about the same field in both comparisons and why DOUBLE is excluded (NaN, signed zero), and unsigned types fail code generation.

user_value.evidence: New physical operator enabled by default; reviewer questioned whether IEJoin plus a residual Calc beats the original join, i.e. whether the rule pays off in the default rule set.

surprising_behavior.evidence: Result row order of inequality joins changes under the default rules; semantics are otherwise the same.

contradictions.evidence: Reviewer found a stale copy-pasted comment in EnumerableIEJoin; covered by doc_comments.

observability.evidence: No logging or metrics relevant to an in-memory join operator.

spec_conformance.evidence: Must match SQL comparison semantics for NULL (excluded), floating point (excluded), and character/datetime keys; handled by restricting types in supportsKeyTypes.

plan.why: A 1500-line new operator with an algorithmic core, planner-cost and default-rule-set impact, and heavy documentation needs; each deserves a focused pass.
